reason: Both answers correctly apply §412: the 3-month grace window has passed, so federal statutory damages and fees are unavailable against this ongoing infringer. Both also note that registration is needed before suing and that actual damages remain available. A adds the Copyright Claims Board route, which allows up to $7,500 in statutory damages despite late registration. That is accurate and could change what the asker does, and A caveats it properly (opt-out, US respondent, offshore pirates). B adds Fourth Estate and the statute of limitations, which matter less. A is slightly better, mainly for the CCB point.
